title: ci(agent-review): review every push to a ready pull request
body:
## What changes

- `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml`: `pull_request` types gain `synchronize`. Every push to an open, ready pull request now starts a Wachiman review. The engine (v1.3.0, unchanged) reviews only what changed since the last reviewed commit, using its incremental marker.
- ADR 0028 gets an amendment: its rejected alternative "Reviewing on every push" is reversed, with the reason and the known costs. The Status row links to it.

## Why

On #475, three of the six valid review findings were on fix commits pushed after the first review, and two were regressions introduced by the fix. Wachiman reviewed only the first commit; Pullfrog and CodeRabbit ran on every push. Analysis: niway-dev/wachiman `docs/benchmark/2026-10-31/pr-475.md` (niway-dev/wachiman#66).

## Known costs until the engine catches up

- A rebase or force-push makes the engine review the whole pull request again (up to the $3 cap).
- No per-pull-request limit yet. A design for one (default $2 of automatic reviews per pull request) is in progress in niway-dev/wachiman.
- A newer push cancels a running review (per-PR concurrency group).
- Thread replies are still read only by the next review run, not answered on their own.

## Checks

- `oxfmt --check` (0.19) on both changed files: passes.
- Not run: `bun run verify:local`. Docs and workflow trigger only.
- To verify after merge: push a commit to an open PR and check that an "Agent review" run starts on `synchronize` and posts "review of changes since `<sha>`".
